title: EPF Withdrawal: Understanding TDS After Five Years of Service

faq.q: What is the minimum service period to avoid TDS on EPF withdrawal?
faq.a: You need to complete five years of continuous service to avoid TDS on your EPF withdrawal.

faq.q: Can I withdraw my EPF if I change jobs?
faq.a: Yes, you can withdraw your EPF if you change jobs, but if it's before five years of continuous service, TDS may apply to amounts over ₹50,000. It's often better to transfer your EPF account to your new employer to maintain continuity of service.

faq.q: What is Form 15G/15H and who can submit it?
faq.a: Form 15G/15H are self-declarations to avoid TDS. Form 15G is for individuals below 60 years, and Form 15H is for senior citizens (60 years and above), provided their total taxable income for the year is below the basic exemption limit.

faq.q: Are partial EPF withdrawals also tax-free?
faq.a: Yes, partial withdrawals (advances) from EPF for specific reasons like medical treatment, education, or house purchase are generally tax-free, irrespective of the service period.

faq.q: What happens if I don't submit Form 15G/15H and withdraw early?
faq.a: If you don't submit Form 15G/15H and withdraw before five years with an amount over ₹50,000, TDS will be deducted by the EPFO. The withdrawn amount will be added to your income and taxed as per your slab during ITR filing.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to link Aadhaar for EPF withdrawal?
faq.a: Yes, for online EPF withdrawal claims, it is mandatory to link and verify your Aadhaar with your UAN.

faq.q: How long does it take to process an EPF withdrawal claim?
faq.a: Online EPF claims are typically processed within 5-10 working days, provided all details are correct and verified. Offline claims may take longer, usually 15-20 days.
